title: Verify how OptiSweep APIs connect to API Dog and Ignition (from the documented API overview)
summary: Use the source-backed mapping to explain which component uses the OptiSweep APIs: OptiSweep provides APIs for “get data” and “make requests,” API Dog is installed on the primary servers, and the same APIs feed Ignition.
when_to_use: Use this when you need a source-backed explanation of the data/request path between OptiSweep APIs, API Dog (on the primary servers), and Ignition, or when you are troubleshooting and need to determine whether observed behavior aligns with the documented mapping.
not_for: Do not use this as a step-by-step diagnostic procedure to validate live API endpoints, request parameters, or response payloads; the source segment provides only the architectural mapping statement and does not include concrete live checks.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Provide the architectural mapping explanation (OptiSweep APIs → API Dog on primary servers; same APIs feed Ignition) and use it to frame troubleshooting discussions.
L2_support: If live behavior does not match the documented mapping, provide deeper support beyond this runbook.
access_or_tools_needed: API Dog (primary servers) access (for explanation/verification, if available)

steps.title: Identify the documented purpose of the OptiSweep APIs (get data / make requests)
steps.purpose: Establish what the OptiSweep APIs are used for so you can correctly interpret the request/data path when explaining system behavior.
steps.instruction: Use the source mapping statement to identify that the OptiSweep “up DB suite” provides APIs used to “get data” and to “make requests.”
steps.expected_result: You can state that the OptiSweep APIs are used for both retrieving data (“get data”) and sending requests (“make requests”).
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation consistently distinguishes between data retrieval (“get data”) and request initiation (“make requests”) as the two documented purposes.
steps.failure_condition: Your explanation omits one of the two documented purposes or reverses their meaning (e.g., treating the APIs as only one of “get data” or “make requests”).

actions.label: Read the API purpose mapping statement
actions.exact_action: APIs up DB suite provides APIs to get data and to make requests.

steps.title: Confirm the documented tooling location: API Dog installed on the primary servers
steps.purpose: Pinpoint where API Dog sits in the documented architecture so you can attribute observed request/data behavior to the correct component.
steps.instruction: Use the source mapping statement to confirm that API Dog is installed on the primary servers.
steps.expected_result: You can state that API Dog is installed on the primary servers.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation places API Dog on the primary servers (not on a consumer/HMI-only side).

steps.title: Confirm the documented integration: the same APIs feed Ignition
steps.purpose: Explain how Ignition consumes the same OptiSweep APIs so you can interpret whether observed behavior is consistent with the documented integration.
steps.instruction: Use the source mapping statement to confirm that the same OptiSweep APIs feed Ignition.
steps.expected_result: You can state that the same APIs feed Ignition.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation connects Ignition as a consumer of the same APIs (not as a separate API provider).
steps.failure_condition: Your explanation treats Ignition as using different APIs than the ones described for OptiSweep “get data” and “make requests.”

steps.title: Use the mapping to attribute observed behavior to API Dog (primary servers) and/or Ignition
steps.purpose: When troubleshooting or explaining system behavior, use the documented mapping to decide which component is likely associated with the observed data/request path.
steps.instruction: When live behavior does not match what you expect from the documented mapping, use the mapping (OptiSweep APIs → API Dog on primary servers; same APIs feed Ignition) to frame whether the observed behavior is associated with API Dog (primary servers) and/or Ignition as the consumer.

steps.healthy_condition: Your attribution references the documented relationship between API Dog and Ignition consuming the same APIs.
